title: Which three numbers can add up to minus eight?
description: Three lift button presses are chosen so that the lift ends on a target floor. Two presses are picked freely, then the third is found from the movement needed to reach the target. The video breaks the slip of thinking only one set of three numbers can work.
teaching_notes: One idea: pick two numbers freely, then find the third as the movement needed, target take away start. Watch for students who think there is only one right set of three numbers.

video_script.why: The child builds three numbers with a given sum by choosing two and finding the third as the movement needed.
video_script.substitution: The lift button presses of the book: starting floor plus movement gives the target floor.
video_script.anchor: the lift of the book with its plus and minus buttons, starting on the ground floor
video_script.payoff_line: One such set of three numbers is minus five, seven and minus ten

final_answer.spoken: minus five, seven and minus ten

never_show: the claim that only one set of three numbers works
maths_rules: (−5) + 7 = 7 − 5 = +2, because the greater number 7 is positive
Target − Starting = Movement: (−8) − (+2) = −10, which is 10 floors down from 2
any two chosen numbers p and q give the third number (−8) − (p + q)
video_script.design: One lift shaft. Two presses are drawn first and the lift stops on a floor, then the third press is drawn to reach the target floor.

<bookmark mark='who'/>Which three numbers could they be?

<bookmark mark='combine'/>Several presses together make one movement, found by adding their numbers.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find three numbers whose sum is minus eight.

beats.on_screen: choose the first two numbers freely: (−5) + 7 = 7 − 5 = +2; the lift stops on floor +2

marks.choose: the first two boxes are filled with −5 and 7
marks.add: the lift goes down 5 floors and up 7 floors and stops on +2

narration: <bookmark mark='choose'/>Step one, choose the first two numbers freely, minus five and seven.
<bookmark mark='add'/>They pull opposite ways, so take five from seven and keep the sign of the greater number.
That gives plus two, so the lift stops on floor two.

beats.on_screen: Target − Starting = Movement; (−8) − (+2) = −10; the lift goes 10 floors down from +2 to −8

marks.rule: the rule Target take away Starting gives Movement is written
marks.sub: the target −8 and the start +2 are filled in
marks.down: the lift goes ten floors down from +2 to −8 and the third box fills with −10

beats.moves_through: the lift moves ten floors down
narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, the third number is the movement needed.
That movement is the target take away the start.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>The target is minus eight and the start is two.
<bookmark mark='down'/>Going from two down to minus eight is ten floors down, so the third number is minus ten.

beats.on_screen: check: (−5) + 7 + (−10) = 2 + (−10) = −8; the lift ends on the target floor −8

marks.check: the three numbers are added from the ground floor
marks.back: the lift stops exactly on floor −8

beats.moves_through: the lift replays all three presses from the ground floor
narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step three, check by adding all three numbers from the ground floor.
<bookmark mark='back'/>Minus five and seven give two, and ten floors down from two is minus eight.

marks.ans: the three numbers are written and boxed
marks.many: the words one of many appear beside the box

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>One such set of three numbers is minus five, seven and minus ten.
<bookmark mark='many'/>Many other sets work too, because the first two numbers can be chosen freely.
